info.title: OTInstaller Registry API
info.summary: The public registry of OSINT tools and guides that ot installs from.
info.description: Public reads need no sign-in and are cached at the edge (Cache-Control says for how long); every JSON read has an ETag, so If-None-Match gets a 304. Errors are {error: {code, message, hint, docs}} (https://otinstaller.com/schema/error-v1.json), with codes at https://otinstaller.com/docs/errors. 429s carry Retry-After. Signed-in calls take an ot_ token as a bearer token; each operation's x-scope names the scope a token needs. Times are Unix milliseconds. Guide: https://otinstaller.com/docs/api

post.description: Anonymous: the ID token is the credential. It must come from GitHub Actions or GitLab.com CI with the audience otinstaller, from a public repository a trusted publisher of the namespace names. Each ID token is exchanged once. The token lasts an hour, acts for the owner who added the publisher, and only uploads (POST /publish) into that namespace and package and follows its job (GET /me/publish-jobs/{id}); anywhere else it counts as anonymous. At most 30 exchanges an hour per repository. Never cached (private, no-store).

post.summary: Upload a release (ot publish): the manifest, its README and pages, and their images
post.description: Needs a sign-in: the session cookie, or an API token with the publish scope, as an owner or publisher of the namespace. One file part per file, named by its path relative to otinstaller.yaml; at most 25 MB and 300 files. The release is then validated, scanned and reviewed as a tag is. At most 20 uploads an hour per namespace.

post.summary: Report a failed run (what ot's prompt sends)
post.description: Only the version, exit code or timeout, OS, architecture, engine and ot version; never inputs or output. With a token it counts as broken for you and joins (or opens) the version's broken issue; without one it only adds to a daily count, shared with the website's broken reports, and enough reports in a week open an unconfirmed issue. Requests with an Origin header other than the registry's website are refused (`foreign_origin`).

post.summary: Report that a tool is broken or out of date, without a sign-in (the tool page's Report a problem)
post.description: Only counted: once per address, version and kind a day, never stored with who sent it. Broken counts join failed runs reported from ot toward the version's unconfirmed issue, opened at three in a week; outdated is always about the latest version and opens its own unconfirmed issue at three in a week, unless the package already has an open outdated issue. Requests with an Origin header other than the registry's website are refused (`foreign_origin`). Signed-in people describe a problem as an issue instead (`POST /tools/{ns}/{name}/issues`).

post.summary: Propose a change to a community package
post.description: The package's maintainers and reviewers. Only files that differ from the wrapper's main branch count. The manifest must validate and keep the package's identity (name, namespace, homepage, license, readme, runtime.kind, and for builds the image the release workflow pins); its version is moved past every version the package had. The Dockerfile follows the submission rules. Secrets refuse a proposal; what looks like personal data is shown to the reviewer. The community bot opens a pull request with the files; a reviewer who isn't the proposer approves it. Three open per person and package, five a day.

post.summary: Merge and release a bump pull request, or release a failed one again
post.description: The package's maintainers (its submitter, others staff add, the namespace's members) and reviewers. The community bot merges the pull request and starts the release: the release workflow for builds (the version follows upstream's), a tag for wheels. A pull request that changes more than the pin needs a reviewer (403 not_pin_only). A bump whose release failed is released again without merging again, under a new version; one being released answers 409 bump_in_progress. If GitHub merged it but the release didn't start, it answers 503 github_failed and the bump can be released again. A first-party tool's dependency update is released the same way, as a patch version. A rebuild on a newer base image has no pull request: it is number 0, and only a failed one can be released again.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events before this Unix time in milliseconds

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Only packages that take this input type, such as email

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: registry: releases, yanks, deprecations, transfers; community: issues confirmed or fixed (issue_confirmed, issue_fixed, with number and issue_kind) and tool requests accepted or published (request_accepted, request_published, with number and tool); all: both. Community events are worded from fields, never from what people wrote.

bearer.description: An ot_ API token from `ot login`, `ot token create` or POST /me/tokens. Tokens have scopes (x-scope on each operation); staff actions need the staff scope, which tokens get only when a signed-in reviewer or admin creates them on the website.

session.name: ot_session
session.description: The website's session (all of the user's powers)

RateLimited.description: Too many requests; retry after Retry-After seconds

Error.title: OTInstaller error, version 1
Error.description: The registry API's error body, and what ot prints on stderr (one line) when JSON output is on. Readers must ignore keys they don't know.

hint.description: What to do next, often an ot command.

exit_code.description: ot only: the exit code ot returns.

request_id.description: Identifies a failed registry request in its logs.

problems.description: Each problem with a manifest or request, most specific first.

notifies_target.description: Present only when the publisher says; unset on a tool that touches the target means it may

items.description: Usually one of the manifest's entity types

egress.description: Tools only: whether runs go online

health_checked_at.description: When the nightly health check last ran, in Unix milliseconds; null when never

sample.description: What the latest version's smoke test produced, when the scanner recorded it: up to five entities for json and jsonl tools, or the first 2000 characters of stdout. The input was the manifest's own test input.

dependencies.description: First-party tools in the community namespace: each exact pin in requirements.txt against PyPI's latest release (the build watcher, nightly)

base_image.description: Docker builds in the community namespace: the final stage's base image and whether its Docker Hub digest changed since the latest version was first seen

rebuilt_at.description: When the registry last started a rebuild of this package

bump.description: The package's current bump of any kind: open, being released, failed, or released in the last two weeks

kind.description: upstream: a community wrapper's pin; dependency: a first-party tool's requirements.txt (version is pkg==1.2,other==3.4); rebuild: the same source built again on a newer base image (number 0, no pull request)

auto_release_at.description: In auto mode, when an open bump goes out on its own (ms)

manifest.description: The manifest without optional fields added after ot v0.12, which older ot rejects

manifest_full.description: The whole manifest; present only when `manifest` leaves fields out

deprecated.description: The package's owner marked it superseded; ot warns on install

descriptions.description: spec/types.json: what each input type, output (entity) type and category means

pivots.description: spec/pivots.json: entity type to the inputs it can feed

unread.description: Unread inbox items, without the kinds you keep out of your inbox

scoped.description: false for tokens from before scopes, which can do everything their user can

indexable.description: Answered by a maintainer, or confirmed or fixed

number.description: The pull request's number in the wrapper repository

version.description: The version the release will have

released_version.description: The version the merge released (the next free one if the proposed one was taken meanwhile)

note.description: The proposer's plain text: show it as text

builds.description: The release workflow builds the image; else a tag releases it

checks.description: What the reviewer should look at: fields_changed, ethics_changed, personal_data and the Dockerfile rules (https://otinstaller.com/docs/errors)

FirstWeek.description: What signed-in people said about a version since it came out, while it is under a week old: counts, never a score

ends_at.description: Unix milliseconds: when the first week ends

changelog.description: The release notes as Markdown, without control characters. Untrusted publisher text: show it as text.

changelog_html.description: The release notes rendered to sanitized HTML, with relative links pointing at the repository at the tagged commit and images replaced by their alt text.

changelog_source.description: release: the host's release for the tag; file: the version's section of CHANGELOG.md (or CHANGES.md, HISTORY.md).

first_week.description: Only while the version is under a week old (list only)

health.description: healthy, broken (possibly broken), unknown or not_checked

source_unavailable.description: The source repository is gone; the package gets no new versions

moved.description: Old addresses of packages that moved, and where they are now

no_keys.description: Packages that need no API key

id.description: Stable for the event; feeds use it as the entry id

new_package.description: published only: the package's first release

has_notes.description: published only: the version has release notes

replacement.description: deprecated only: the package to use instead

first_week.description: published only, while the version is under a week old
